title: Power Platform: secure Dataverse records with column-based filtering
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts and documented preview controls are supported. Minor corrections should identify the existing Dataverse licensing entitlement, complete the security-role path, name the API request properties, and cite the supporting API example and ALM guidance.

claims.claim: This roadmap change concerns Power Platform governance and administration and securing Dataverse records with column-based filtering.
claims.quote: Microsoft Power Platform governance and administration: Secure Dataverse record with column-based filtering

claims.claim: The enhancement secures records using column attribute values rather than traditional ownership.
claims.quote: This enhancement introduces column-based security filtering, enabling records to be secured using attribute values rather than traditional ownership.

claims.claim: Security administrators can define access by business dimensions such as region or department.
claims.quote: This allows security admins to define access based on business dimensions such as region or department

claims.claim: The change targets scenarios without natural record ownership, including reporting and aggregated datasets.
claims.quote: making it ideal for scenarios where record ownership does not exist—such as reporting and aggregated datasets.

claims.claim: Avoiding artificial ownership or complex sharing models simplifies administration and improves scalability.
claims.quote: By eliminating the need for artificial ownership or complex sharing models, this approach simplifies security administration, improves scalability

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate / What's changing / Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap target is January CY2027, not a confirmed general availability date.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds / What's changing / Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap cloud scope is Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: Sovereign-cloud availability for this change is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse "filter-based security" "577860" sovereign clouds; read roadmap clouds and the admin, maker and developer filter-security guides. No feature-specific sovereign availability statement found.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents filter-based security as a preview.
claims.quote: This feature is in preview.

claims.where: What's changing / Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Record Filters define qualifying records using FetchXML.
claims.quote: Record Filter: Uses FetchXML to identify records that qualify for access.

claims.claim: Entity Record Filters associate Record Filters with Dataverse tables.
claims.quote: Entity Record Filter: Associates a Record Filter with a Dataverse table.

claims.claim: Filter privileges are granted through security roles assigned to users or teams.
claims.quote: Select the target table. ... Select the filter privilege. ... Grant the privilege to the role. ... Assign the role to users or teams.

claims.where: What's changing / Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Filtered record ownership tables have no record owner.
claims.quote: Filtered ownership tables don't use record owners.

claims.claim: Filters can also be added to user or team-owned and organization-owned tables.
claims.quote: You can apply filter-based security to user or team, and organization record ownership, and filtered record ownership tables.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure / Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: On user-owned tables, filter privileges add access and do not reduce ownership-based access.
claims.quote: For user or team record ownership tables, filter privileges add row-level access to ownership-based security. They don't replace or reduce access granted through ownership, sharing, or security role privileges.

claims.claim: Filtered ownership records cannot be shared with users or teams.
claims.quote: Can't be shared with users or teams.

claims.claim: Filtered ownership records cannot be assigned to users or teams.
claims.quote: Can't be assigned to users or teams.

claims.claim: Creating a filtered ownership table automatically gives System Administrator an All records privilege.
claims.quote: When you create a filtered record ownership table, Dataverse creates a global All records filter privilege and grants it to the System Administrator security role.

claims.where: Why it matters / Risk assessment: Change & support / Governance guidance
claims.claim: Effective filter access combines privileges from users' assigned roles and team memberships.
claims.quote: Dataverse combines all authorized filters from the user's security roles and team memberships. A record that matches any authorized filter receives the corresponding access.

claims.claim: Configuring the preview feature and its security roles requires the System Administrator security role.
claims.quote: A user with the system administrator security role must configure the feature and security roles.

claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in because an administrator must configure filters and role privileges to use it.
claims.quote: A user with the system administrator security role must configure the feature and security roles. ... After creating the record filter and entity record filter, grant the filter for the required Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append, or Append to table privileges in a security role.

claims.claim: Power Apps > environment > Solutions > solution > New table > Table (advanced properties) > Record ownership > Filtered (preview) creates a filtered ownership table in the selected environment.
claims.quote: Select your environment. ... Go to Solutions, open the solution you want or create a new one. ... Select New table on the command bar, and then select Table (advanced properties). ... From the Record ownership list, select Filtered (preview).

claims.claim: Record Filters are created separately in a solution using + New > More > Other > Record Filter.
claims.quote: Go to Solutions and create a new solution or open an existing solution. ... Select + New. ... Select More and Other. ... Select Record Filter.

claims.claim: EntityRecordFilter is a separate solution item created after the Record Filter.
claims.quote: Return to your Solution. ... Select + New. ... Select More and Other. ... Select EntityRecordFilter. ... Select the Record Filter, such as City of Redmond.

claims.claim: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/recordfilters creates a Record Filter with a request body rather than creating a table.
claims.quote: Create a recordfilter row. ... POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/recordfilters HTTP/1.1 ... "fetchxml": "<fetch><entity name=\"new_store\"><filter type=\"and\">
claims.fix: Remove ', each with a request body' from controls[0].api.call and the rendered call. Add this sentence to controls[0].note and the rendered note: 'The recordfilters request body sets fetchxml.' Keep the documented endpoint unchanged.

claims.claim: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/entityrecordfilters associates a Record Filter with a table using a request body rather than creating a table.
claims.quote: Use the RecordFilterId single-valued navigation property to associate the record filter. ... POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/entityrecordfilters HTTP/1.1 ... "objecttypecode": "new_store", "RecordFilterId@odata.bind": "/recordfilters(
claims.fix: Keep the entityrecordfilters endpoint unchanged and add this sentence to controls[0].note and the rendered note: 'The entityrecordfilters request body sets objecttypecode to the table logical name and RecordFilterId@odata.bind to the Record Filter.'

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles > role reaches the role whose filter privileges are configured.
claims.quote: Select Manage on the navigation pane. ... select Environments and then select an environment. ... select Settings. ... Expand Users + permissions and select Security roles. ... Choose the security role you want to edit.
claims.fix: The path stops early on the correct page. Set controls[1].ui.path and the rendered path to 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles > role > target table > filter privilege'. The last two selections are documented at the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/filter-based-security#grant-filter-privileges-in-security-roles.

claims.claim: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/roles(<roleid>)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddPrivilegesRole adds existing privileges to an existing role using a Privileges collection of RolePrivilege values.
claims.quote: Pass the list as the AddPrivilegesRole.Privileges parameter. ... POST [Organization Uri]/api/data/v9.2/roles(44ee44ee-ff55-aa66-bb77-88cc88cc88cc)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddPrivilegesRole HTTP/1.1
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/web-api-functions-actions-sample#section-8-bound-action-addprivilegesrole to sources for the full versioned invocation. Set controls[1].api.call and the rendered call to 'POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/roles(<roleid>)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddPrivilegesRole'. Add to the row note: 'The request body supplies a Privileges collection of RolePrivilege values.' The existing AddPrivilegesRole docs link supports the bound action and parameter; the pre-check's missing literal POST is not a nonexistent operation.

claims.claim: RolePrivilege has a RecordFilterId property.
claims.quote: RecordFilterId | Edm.Guid | The Record Filter of the privilege.

claims.claim: RolePrivilege has a RecordFilterUniqueName property.
claims.quote: RecordFilterUniqueName | Edm.String | The Unique Name for the Record Filter of the privilege.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no tenant-wide availability switch for filter-based security on either UI or API surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse "filter-based security" tenant enable switch preview rollout; "filter-based security" "tenant" "switch" API. Opened admin/filter-based-security and maker/developer filtered ownership guides; none documents a tenant-wide UI or API switch.

claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown, with no feature-specific entitlement published.
claims.quote: Users can create custom tables with Dynamics 365, Power Apps, or Power Automate license
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Set licensing.notes to 'Existing Dataverse table licensing applies: users can create custom tables with a Dynamics 365, Power Apps, or Power Automate license. No licence specific to filter-based security is published as of November 2026.' The cited page states the product-level requirement, not a separate feature entitlement.

claims.claim: No separate licence or licence change specific to filter-based security is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse "filtered record ownership" licensing pricing general availability. Read the admin, maker and developer feature guides, License requirements for tables, and Licensing overview search results; no separate feature licence found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes / Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Existing Dataverse table licensing requirements apply.
claims.quote: App makers can use most of the tables available within Microsoft Dataverse (including custom tables and tables that are part of the Common Data Model) to create apps and flows for users who have a Power Apps or Power Automate license.

claims.claim: Dataverse capacity applies to these tables as to other Dataverse tables.
claims.quote: All Dataverse tables, including system tables, are included in the storage capacity reports. ... Database only: All other tables count for your database

claims.claim: Feature-specific general availability pricing has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse "filtered record ownership" licensing pricing general availability. Read feature guides, License requirements for tables and Dataverse capacity-based storage details, plus Licensing overview search results; no feature-specific GA price found.

claims.claim: An explicit identification of roadmap item 577860 with the documented preview was not found.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse "filter-based security" "577860" sovereign clouds. Read roadmap record (moreInfoLink null), admin/filter-based-security, maker/filtered-view-record-ownership and developer/filtered-record-ownership; no explicit roadmap-to-preview identification found.

claims.claim: Preview enablement and rollout mechanics beyond the documented configuration procedure are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "filtered record ownership" "enable" "preview" environment settings; Dataverse "filter-based security" tenant enable switch preview rollout. Opened admin, maker and developer feature guides; no preview rollout or enablement procedure beyond configuration found.

claims.claim: Record Filters and Entity Record Filters are solution components.
claims.quote: All solution components created by the examples are associated with this solution. ... MSCRM.SolutionUniqueName: <Solution Unique Name>

claims.claim: Solution components can travel with solutions through application lifecycle management deployments.
claims.quote: Solutions are the mechanism for implementing application lifecycle management (ALM) in Power Apps and Power Automate. ... The purpose of having components is ... so that it can be exported, imported
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/alm/solution-concepts-alm to sources for the existing statement that solution components travel with solutions through ALM deployments.

claims.claim: Creating the table or filter records alone does not grant filtered access without a security role holding the filter privilege.
claims.quote: After creating the record filter and entity record filter, grant the filter for the required Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append, or Append to table privileges in a security role. Assign the role to users or teams.

claims.claim: This feature is an access-control model rather than an autonomous action capability.
claims.quote: When a user accesses data, Dataverse evaluates the filters from the user's security roles and team memberships. A matching filter grants the corresponding data access operation.

claims.claim: For filtered ownership tables, filters are the exclusive basis for record access instead of ownership-based privileges.
claims.quote: Only filtered record ownership tables rely exclusively on filter privileges for record access. ... Don't use ownership-based security privileges.

controlChecks.governs: Tables with filtered record ownership and their record filters
